1.explanation:
To understand and reproduce this issue, you need to see how the Tabs container and individual Tab components are implemented and how they set up ARIA attributes for assistive technology. 

• Tab/index.js and Tab/Tab.js contain the Tab component’s role, aria-selected and (where applicable) the aria-posinset/aria-setsize attributes that tell a screen reader a tab’s position in its group. 
• Tabs/index.js and Tabs/Tabs.js implement the Tabs container that iterates over its Tab children and should pass down the total number of tabs (aria-setsize) and each tab’s index (aria-posinset). 
• TabContent/index.js and TabContent/TabContent.js link each tab to its panel via aria-controls and aria-labelledby, completing the accessibility relationship between the tab list and its content. 

By reviewing these files you can verify whether the aria-posinset and aria-setsize props are correctly calculated and applied—and why VoiceOver always hears “1 of 1.”
1.bug_scenario: In the default Tabs story there are four tabs (“Tab label 1” through “Tab label 4” and a custom‐labeled tab). When VoiceOver is turned on and you navigate between these tabs, the screen reader always reports “tab, 1 of 1” for the focused tab—even though there are clearly multiple tabs. Visually, you can see the focus ring and selected styling move correctly, but VoiceOver never announces the correct total number of tabs in the group.
